messages.subject: Re: mentoring for Google Code-In?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, hope you'll are doing well.
I was a Student Developer in the Google Summer of Code 2019 with INCF and am eager to apply for mentoring Google Code in 2019 projects. I also use the R programming language often at work as a Software Developer with HSBC, UK.
Could you please point me the right way?
Thank you!

On Wednesday, October 16, 2019 at 11:08:33 PM UTC+5:30, tdh...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi GSOC mentors,
>
> I am working on an application for R project in Google Code-In, which is similar to GSOC, but for high school students. The project ideas need to be small tasks (each doable in about a day) suitable for high school students. No developing new R packages from scratch. But some appropriate ideas would be
> - closing issues
> - fixing simple bugs
> - updating documentation
> - setting up pkgdown web pages for projects that don't already have it
> - setting up CI for projects that don't already have it
> etc
>
> Mentor responsibilities are listed on
> https://developers.google.com/open-source/gci/help/responsibilities#mentor_responsibilities
>
> If you would be interested to participate as a mentor, can you please write me an email, so I can get an idea about how many mentors with previous GSOC experience may be available?

messages.subject: Update on GCI for Mentors and Students
messages.subject_clean: Update on GCI for Mentors and Students
messages.body_plain:
Hello Everyone,

As we all know this year, The R Project for the first time is participating in GCI program. So people who are still not aware about what Google Code-In-Program is, click here: https://codein.withgoogle.com/

For Students:
1. Kindly join our gitter channel for easier communication:   https://gitter.im/rstats-gci/gci-student
Kindly wait if response is late, but we will surely respond to your queries as soon as possible. If not, you can mail us.

2. All the tasks will be published on 2nd December, before that, you can have a sneak peak to the task here: https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gci2019/wiki/Tasks-for-students [ Remember, you don't have to start now or submit it anywhere else, all the submission will happen of GCI dashboard which will be reviewed by your mentors for that particular task.]

For Mentors:

Thank you for taking out time and mentoring students. I humbly request you to add more common tasks, those who want to add ideas are welcome too.
Link to add common tasks: https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gci2019/wiki/Common-Task-Information

I also request all mentors to start migrating your tasks from ( https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gci2019/wiki/Tasks-for-students ) to (https://codein.withgoogle.com/dashboard/tasks/) This is very important part, we need to publish as many tasks possible for students.

I request you to create smaller task in the beginning and then move to higher level considering this will be 13 to 17 year old students who might not have knowledge of R and will be starting for the first time.  So as many beginner task as possible, they can be related to your project or not.

For Mentors Interested:

We have been getting queries about how to participate as a mentor. We are excited to see a great response and welcome you to the mentorship program.
Kindly send a mail to @Toby Hocking or @kr.vivek.ab with your previous projects (package or cran) or if you have worked extensively in R and open source before. Bullet-points will do with a project link.

Feel free to reach out to me @Toby Hocking for any questions. Looking forward to GCI.

Thanks,
Vivek
